transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... most nights, when my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen. And I just eat way past a normal plate. I'll get into whatever event leftovers are in there—like fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls, whatever it is—and I just keep going until a whole tray or, you know, half the fridge is completely gone.
After one of these eating episodes, do you ever try to 'undo' it—like making yourself vomit, taking laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never... I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise to work it off. I just sort of... deal with feeling really full and miserable afterwards. But no, I don't try to undo it.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly it. It's like... once I take that very first bite, it feels like the decision has already been made for me. I really can't stop. Even while I'm standing there literally telling myself, 'George, stop now,' my hands just keep going. They just keep fixing another plate or opening up another container. I just have no control over it once I start.
Do these episodes happen after you've already fallen asleep and then wake up to go eat, or do they happen in the evening before you've gone to sleep at all?
They happen before I've gone to sleep. I'm usually still awake, just up by myself after my wife has already gone to bed. I haven't fallen asleep yet when it happens.
How many nights per week does this happen, and how long has this pattern been going on?

It happens pretty often. For months now, I honestly can't think of a single week where it didn't happen at least once. And most weeks... it's been several nights, usually right after my wife goes to bed. It's just been this ongoing pattern for a while now.
After one of these eating episodes, how do you feel emotionally—do you experience guilt, shame, or significant distress about what happened?

Yeah, I definitely do. Afterward, I just feel sick with myself. It's like... everybody sees me as this organized and strong man, but then I'm just sitting there feeling completely ashamed and guilty. I just feel disgusted that I let it happen all over again.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control, occurring multiple times per week for several months. He denies any compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise, ruling out bulimia nervosa. He is fully awake before going to sleep (not after waking from sleep), which does not fit the classic Night Eating Syndrome pattern of eating after nocturnal awakenings, but the behavior is closely tied to a nighttime routine (after his wife goes to bed). The episodes cause marked guilt, shame, and distress. Because ICD-10 (WHO) does not have a distinct code for Binge Eating Disorder, and the presentation includes atypical timing (evening/pre-sleep rather than classic daytime binge or nocturnal awakening pattern), this is best classified as an Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (F50.8), capturing a binge-eating-type disorder with atypical or insufficient features to meet full bulimia nervosa criteria and not perfectly matching night eating syndrome due to no post-sleep awakening.
